deals.evidence: with Belgian entrepreneur Roland Duchâtelet acquiring 100 per cent of the club
deals.headline: Roland Duchâtelet acquires 100% of Charlton Athletic
deals.summary: Belgian entrepreneur Roland Duchâtelet bought 100% of the club on 3 January 2014 (before the 2015 window; included because he still owns The Valley).

deals.evidence: Duchâtelet sold Charlton to East Street Investments for just £1 in January 2020
deals.headline: Duchâtelet sells Charlton to East Street Investments for £1
deals.summary: Duchâtelet sold the club, but not The Valley or the training ground, to East Street Investments for £1; the consortium collapsed amid in-fighting later in 2020. Companies House records ESI as the controlling shareholder from 23 January 2020.

deals.evidence: Sandgaard completed his acquisition of 100% ownership of the club in September 2020
deals.headline: Thomas Sandgaard completes takeover of Charlton
deals.summary: Danish-American businessman Thomas Sandgaard completed the acquisition of 100% of the club in September 2020 through Clear Ocean Capital Limited; the Valley and training ground leases were amended to 15-year terms on 25 September 2020.

deals.evidence: GFP paid around £15m for Charlton three years ago
deals.headline: Global Football Partners buys Charlton from Thomas Sandgaard for around £15m
deals.summary: SE7 Partners, the UK subsidiary of Global Football Partners (led by Gabriel Brener, with Joshua Friedman, Warren Rosenfeld, ACA Football Partners and others), completed the purchase of Charlton Athletic and Charlton Athletic Women; the price is reported as around £15m.

deals.evidence: Charlton Athletic’s decision to extend its lease at both The Valley and Sparrows Lane until 2040
deals.headline: Charlton extend leases on The Valley and Sparrows Lane to 2040
deals.summary: The club extended its leases at The Valley and the Sparrows Lane training ground to June 2040, six seasons beyond the previous terms; the ground remains owned by Roland Duchâtelet. No rent was disclosed.

name: Charlton Athletic Football Club
notes: The Companies House accounts PDF is a scanned image: evidence strings were transcribed from the page and a text search of the PDF will not find them. The 2024/25 accounts carry a qualified audit opinion because a ransomware attack in August 2024 wiped the legacy accounting system. 2024/25 was a League One season (promoted via the play-offs); attendance is the club's 2025/26 Championship figure (2024/25 per the accounts: 15,255). Stakes within Global Football Partners are only described as 5%+ each, so stake_pct is null; the shareholder list is as published at the July 2023 takeover and may have changed. Stadium: The Guardian (August 2026) and Inside World Football say Roland Duchâtelet still owns The Valley; note that Companies House shows Duchâtelet ceasing to control Charlton Athletic Holdings Limited and Baton 2010 Limited (registered at The Valley) on 16 February 2026, Baton 2010 now reporting no registrable controller, which no press read explains. August 2026: GFP appointed Oakwell Sports Advisory to find investment or a buyer (Guardian); chair Gavin Carter called it a search for investment, not a sale. No valuation, chief executive, social counts or honours found on a citable page.

ownership_summary: Global Football Partners Limited (Cayman Islands) owns the club through its UK subsidiary SE7 Partners Limited, having bought it from Thomas Sandgaard in July 2023 for around £15m. At the takeover GFP had seven shareholders with 5%+ each (the Brener, Friedman and Rosenfeld families, Singapore's ACA Football Partners, Munir Javeri, Marc Boyan and Charlie Methven) plus smaller holders; it is led by Gabriel Brener and Joshua Friedman (Canyon Partners). The accounts state there is no ultimate controlling party. In August 2026 GFP engaged Oakwell Sports Advisory to seek new investment or a buyer.
